title: Unify variant token fallbacks and motion-reduction presets for button theming
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Consolidate per-variant token fallback rules and introduce a small set of motion-reduction presets that the Button component consumes across themes (light, dark, high-contrast, console-theme). Motivation: We have several recurring regressions where a missing semantic token in a customer's theme causes visible color/contrast breakage for secondary/ghost variants, and inconsistent spinner placement/animation timing across themes causes perceived jitter during fast interactions. This ticket unblocks a hardening pass for button variants (primary/secondary/ghost/destructive/outlined/icon-only) and makes motion behavior accessible-by-default.
acceptance_criteria: Button component reads a documented fallback chain for each semantic token (foreground/pressed/disabled/border/spinner) and exposes it as a single source of truth in tokens.ts
Spinner placement and size are deterministic per variant and do not shift layout (icon overlap or label masking must be covered), validated with visual-diff snapshots across themes
Motion-reduction presets (none, reduced, minimal) are plumbed from the theme/context and used to switch animation durations/easing for 90% of button micro-interactions
No contrast regressions in high-contrast theme (WCAG 4.5 simulated) for any variant at normal and disabled states
Unit tests for token fallback logic and storybook stories for each theme/variant combination exist and pass in CI
A/B rollout plan defined: start with internal console routes, then progressive rollout to 10% of public users behind a feature flag
constraints_and_tradeoffs: We will avoid adding per-customer theme overrides in this ticket; fallback is deterministic and local to the DS runtime to keep bundle size small
Some legacy consumers relied on implicit layout shifts; we will provide a compatibility shim for one release (ds-legacy-shim) and document the migration path
Motion presets are intentionally coarse to reduce API surface; if customers need finer control we will follow up with an opt-in prop in a later ticket
design_notes: Prototype includes three motion presets and visual examples showing spinner overlay vs inline spinner for icon-only buttons
implementation_plan: 1) Add token fallback table in src/tokens/buttonTokens.ts and expose as a small JSON map consumed by button style engine
2) Implement motion presets in src/theme/motion-presets.ts and wire into ThemeProvider; default to 'reduced' when prefers-reduced-motion is set
3) Adjust Button component: reserve label width when spinner appears (avoid layout shift), unify spinner color selection to use computed foreground token
4) Add Storybook matrix (variant x theme x motion) and automated Percy/Chromatic snapshots
5) Regression test on Console and Dedicated UI routes, roll behind feature flag for 10% traffic
risks: Potential visual regressions in a small set of legacy apps that rely on previous implicit fallbacks
Edge cases where third-party theme providers define tokens with unexpected formats; mitigated by strict validation and telemetry to detect malformed tokens
Slight bundle size increase (~1.2KB gzipped) from token map; acceptable tradeoff for deterministic behavior
qa_plan: Manual QA: iterate through storybook matrix, confirm spinner placement and contrast in light/dark/high-contrast
Automated: visual-diff snapshots added to CI, unit tests for fallback selection logic, simulate prefers-reduced-motion in browser tests
Performance: measure initial render and interaction latency in Console routes to ensure no measurable regressions
rollout_and_monitoring: Phase 1: internal-only feature flag for Console team (2 days)
Phase 2: progressive rollout to 10% public traffic for 48 hours with dashboards to track visual-diff failures and SLOs
Fallback: quick rollback via feature flag and revert PR if > 3 visual-diff unexpected failures or customer tickets marked high-impact
